why: DPDP Section 5 (notice) and Section 6 (consent must be free, specific, informed, unambiguous and given by a clear affirmative action, for a specified purpose) require the hospital to present an understandable notice and capture valid, purpose-bound consent in the patient's language — and to keep every version provable.

features.name: Purpose-Based Consent Capture
features.description: Capture consent split into discrete, independently-toggled purposes (treatment, diagnostics sharing, research) rather than one blanket form.
features.userStory: As front-desk staff, I want to capture consent broken out by purpose so that each downstream use has its own provable basis under DPDP.
acceptanceCriteria: Each purpose is an independent opt-in; bundled or blanket consent is not possible.
Required vs optional purposes are visually distinct and no purpose defaults to ON.
Each captured consent records purpose, data categories, timestamp and the notice version shown.
A patient can grant some purposes and decline others and still complete the flow.

features.name: Vernacular Notice & Consent
features.description: Present the notice and consent in the patient's chosen language (English + Eighth-Schedule languages), language chosen before anything else.
features.userStory: As a patient, I want the notice and consent in my own language so that I actually understand what I am agreeing to.
acceptanceCriteria: Language is selected before any notice text is shown.
v1 ships English, Hindi and at least two regional languages.
The exact language version shown is stored with the consent record.
Switching language never changes the scope or purposes being captured.

features.name: Assisted & Kiosk Capture for OPD
features.description: Low-literacy-friendly capture on a shared tablet/kiosk, self-serve or staff-assisted, designed for an OPD waiting room.
features.userStory: As front-desk staff, I want to capture consent on a shared device for a patient who can barely use a phone so that nobody is excluded or pushed back to paper.
acceptanceCriteria: A consent completed on a staff-operated device is still attributed to the patient after patient verification.
Interface offers large touch targets, icon-led purposes and a read-aloud option.
A standard OPD consent completes in roughly 90 seconds.
Staff-assisted sessions record that assistance was given and by whom.

features.name: Identity-Bound Signature (ABHA / OTP)
features.description: Bind each consent to a verified identity via ABHA or mobile OTP and sign it with Certinal eSign.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want every consent bound to a verified patient identity so that it holds up as that specific person's affirmative action.
acceptanceCriteria: Consent is signed via Certinal eSign and bound to a verified identifier (ABHA where available, else OTP-verified mobile).
The signed artifact is immutable once captured.
The identity-verification method used is recorded on the consent.
An unverified consent cannot reach 'active' status.

features.name: Version Tracking & Re-Consent
features.description: Every notice or purpose change creates a new immutable version; materially affected patients are flagged for re-consent.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want every consent version preserved and changes to trigger re-consent so that we can always prove which version a patient agreed to.
acceptanceCriteria: Editing a notice or purpose set creates a new version; prior versions are never overwritten.
Each consent records the exact version the patient agreed to.
A material change flags impacted patients for re-consent.
Superseded consents are marked as such, not deleted.

features.name: Queryable Consent Repository
features.description: A central, searchable store of all consents with status, purpose, language, version and validity.
features.userStory: As compliance, I want to search every consent by patient, purpose or status so that I can answer 'what did this patient agree to' instantly.
acceptanceCriteria: Search by patient/ABHA, purpose, status and date range.
Each record shows purpose, language, version, validity window and current status.
A single patient's full consent set exports in one action.
Results return in seconds, not minutes.

features.name: Consent Expiry & Validity Windows
features.description: Time-bound or event-bound consents that lapse automatically rather than living forever.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want consents to carry validity windows so that processing doesn't continue indefinitely on an old consent.
acceptanceCriteria: A consent can be fixed-term or event-bound (e.g. 'until discharge').
Expired consents move to inactive automatically.
Expiring consents trigger a renewal prompt within a configurable lead time.

features.name: Guardian / Minor Consent
features.description: Capture consent given by a verified guardian for a minor or dependent, per DPDP's provisions for children.
features.userStory: As front-desk staff, I want to capture a parent's consent for a minor so that we lawfully process a child's data.
acceptanceCriteria: Guardian identity and relationship are recorded and the grant is flagged as guardian-given.
Guardian verification is attached to the consent evidence.
Grants for minors can be configured to require re-consent when the child reaches majority.

why: DPDP Section 7 purpose limitation and Section 8(1) accountability require a Data Fiduciary to ensure all processing is backed by valid, purpose-scoped permission and to prove it on demand, so the hospital needs an enforceable execution layer — route, scope, enforce at point-of-use, and evidence — not just stored consent.

features.name: Purpose-Scoped Grant Builder
features.description: Defines every authorization as a structured grant bound to a specific purpose, data categories, and time/expiry window so processing can never exceed what the patient permitted.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want every authorization to be tied to a named purpose, specific data categories, and an expiry so that processing is provably limited to what the patient agreed to under DPDP purpose limitation.
acceptanceCriteria: A grant cannot be created without at least one named purpose, one or more data categories, and a validity window (fixed end-date or event-based, e.g. 'until discharge').
Selecting a purpose auto-constrains the selectable data categories to those declared necessary for that purpose; out-of-scope categories cannot be added.
Each grant shows a human-readable scope summary ('Cardiology can view labs + imaging for treatment until 31-Dec-2026') visible to staff and patient.
A grant past its expiry or event trigger automatically moves to an inactive state with no further processing allowed.

features.name: Configurable Multi-Party Approval Routing
features.description: Routes an authorization request through an ordered or parallel set of approvers (clinician, DPO/ethics, patient) with rules that vary by use-case and data sensitivity.
features.userStory: As a hospital admin, I want to configure who must approve which type of request so that sensitive data sharing always gets the right sign-offs before any data moves.
acceptanceCriteria: Admins can build a routing rule specifying approvers, order (sequential or parallel), and conditions (purpose, data category, requester role) without code.
A request cannot reach 'granted' state until every required approver in the active route has acted.
Patient approval can be inserted as a mandatory step in any route, and the patient's decision is binding (a clinician cannot override a patient denial).
Each approver sees the exact scope they are approving, and a rejection at any step halts the request with a recorded reason.

features.name: Use-Case Workflow Templates
features.description: Prebuilt, editable templates for the common Indian healthcare authorization scenarios — treatment, insurance/TPA claim, caregiver access, external data share, and research — so each use-case ships with correct routing, scope, and notices.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want ready-made templates per use-case so that front-line teams launch compliant authorizations without reinventing scope and routing each time.
acceptanceCriteria: V1 ships with at least four templates: insurance/TPA, caregiver/family access, external data share, and research/ethics.
Each template pre-fills purpose, default data categories, validity, and the required approver route, and remains editable before launch.
Selecting a template enforces its mandatory steps (e.g. research template forces a DPO/ethics approval step that cannot be removed).
Templates are versioned so the exact template version used for any grant is recoverable later.

features.name: Point-of-Use Enforcement Check
features.description: A real-time permission check that EMR/HIS and downstream systems call before any data access or share, returning allow/block based on the live grant — turning permission into enforcement, not paperwork.
features.userStory: As a clinician, I want the system to tell me in real time whether I'm permitted to access or share a patient's data so that I never act outside what the patient authorized.
acceptanceCriteria: A data-use attempt is evaluated against the active grant's purpose, data category, requester, and validity, returning a clear allow or block decision.
If no valid grant exists or the requested use falls outside scope, the action is blocked and the reason is shown to the user.
An expired, withdrawn, or out-of-window grant produces a block even if the data was previously accessible.
Every check (allow and block) is recorded with timestamp, requester, purpose, and outcome.

features.name: SLA Timers and Escalation
features.description: Tracks how long each approval step has been pending and auto-escalates or reassigns when an approver misses the SLA, so authorizations don't silently stall.
features.userStory: As a hospital admin, I want stalled approval steps to escalate automatically so that patient care and claims aren't held up by an unresponsive approver.
acceptanceCriteria: Each route step has a configurable time limit, and a breach triggers escalation to a defined backup approver or role.
Pending and breached requests are visible in a queue filterable by approver, use-case, and age.
Escalations and reassignments are logged with timestamps and the triggering rule.
Approvers receive reminders before the SLA breaches via their configured channel.

features.name: Guardian and Delegated Authorization
features.description: Handles authorizations granted by a verified guardian for a minor or by a delegate/caregiver for an incapacitated adult, binding the grant to the delegate's verified identity and relationship.
features.userStory: As front-desk staff, I want to capture and route an authorization given by a parent or caregiver so that we lawfully process a minor's or dependent's data under DPDP guardian-consent rules.
acceptanceCriteria: A grant for a minor or dependent records the guardian/delegate identity, the relationship, and the basis of authority.
The grant flags it was given by a guardian/delegate (not the principal directly) wherever the grant is viewed.
Guardian-based grants tied to a minor can be configured to require re-authorization upon the principal reaching majority.
The delegate's verified identity (e.g. via ABHA where available) is attached to the grant evidence.

features.name: Re-Authorization and Renewal Workflows
features.description: Detects grants nearing expiry, scope changes, or purpose changes and runs a lightweight re-consent/renewal loop rather than letting processing continue on stale permission.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want expiring or scope-changed grants to trigger a renewal request so that we never keep processing data on an out-of-date or expanded purpose.
acceptanceCriteria: Grants approaching expiry generate a renewal request to the patient and relevant approvers within a configurable lead time.
Adding a new purpose or data category to an existing grant triggers a fresh authorization rather than silently expanding scope.
If a renewal is not completed before expiry, the grant lapses to inactive and point-of-use checks begin blocking.
The renewal links to the prior grant so the full lineage of a continuing authorization is traceable.

features.name: Cross-Fiduciary External Share Approval
features.description: A specialized route for sharing data with a third party (TPA, pharma sponsor, referral hospital, research collaborator) that captures the recipient, onward-use purpose, and transfer conditions before release.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want external data shares to go through a dedicated approval that records the recipient and their permitted onward use so that we retain accountability after data leaves our systems.
acceptanceCriteria: An external-share request requires a named recipient, the recipient's permitted purpose, and the data categories being shared.
Release is blocked until the external-share route is fully approved, including a DPO step.
The share record captures the transfer scope and any onward-use restrictions for later inspection.
Each external share is individually traceable to the patient grant that authorized it.

why: DPDP Section 6(4)-(6) requires that a Data Principal be able to withdraw consent "as easily as it was given," that the Data Fiduciary cease processing within a reasonable time, and that this cascade to its Data Processors — so a hospital needs an execution-and-evidence layer that turns a withdrawal request into completed stop/purge actions across every system and downstream party that holds the affected data.

features.name: Omnichannel Withdrawal Intake
features.description: Capture a withdrawal request through any channel the patient already uses — self-service portal/app, front-desk assisted, or phone — into a single tracked request.
features.userStory: As a patient, I want to withdraw my consent through the portal, the front desk, or a phone call so that I can stop processing of my data using whichever channel is easiest for me.
acceptanceCriteria: A patient can initiate withdrawal from the self-service portal/app without staff involvement, and the same request can alternatively be logged by front-desk staff or a phone agent on the patient's behalf.
Every withdrawal request, regardless of channel, produces one unified request record with a unique reference number shown/read back to the patient.
The withdrawal entry point is reachable in no more steps than the original consent capture (verifiable parity test of clicks/steps), satisfying 'as easy to withdraw as to give'.
Assisted (front-desk/phone) withdrawals require patient identity verification (e.g., ABHA/OTP or in-person ID) before the request is accepted.

features.name: Partial vs Full Withdrawal Selector
features.description: Let the patient withdraw consent for specific purposes (e.g., research, marketing) while retaining others (e.g., active treatment), in plain language.
features.userStory: As a patient, I want to withdraw consent for some purposes (like research or marketing) but keep consent for my ongoing treatment so that I stay in control without disrupting my care.
acceptanceCriteria: The patient sees each active consent purpose as a separately selectable item and can withdraw one, several, or all of them in a single request.
Purposes that are legally required to continue (e.g., statutory medical record retention) are clearly flagged as not withdrawable, with the reason stated.
Purpose names and descriptions are shown in the patient's chosen language (Eighth Schedule set) at the point of selection.
The resulting request explicitly records which purposes are withdrawn and which are retained.

features.name: Withdrawal Impact Analysis
features.description: Automatically map a withdrawal to every internal system, dataset, and downstream party (processors, labs, third parties) that holds the affected data.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want a withdrawal request to automatically show me which systems and external parties hold the affected data so that I know exactly what must stop or be purged.
acceptanceCriteria: On submission, the system generates an impact list of internal systems/datasets and named downstream parties linked to the withdrawn purpose(s).
Each impacted item shows its responsible owner and the required action (stop processing vs purge vs notify downstream).
Retained-purpose data and legally-retained data are excluded from purge actions and shown separately so they are not wrongly deleted.
The DPO can review the impact list before tasks are dispatched.

features.name: Task Routing with SLA Deadlines
features.description: Route each stop/purge/notify action to the responsible system owner as a tracked task with a due date and escalation if missed.
features.userStory: As a hospital admin, I want each withdrawal action routed to the right system owner with a deadline so that processing actually stops within the legally required time, not just on paper.
acceptanceCriteria: Each impacted item generates a task assigned to its owner with a configurable SLA due date derived from the withdrawal date.
Tasks approaching or past their deadline trigger reminders and escalate to a supervisor/DPO.
A live dashboard shows, per withdrawal, how many tasks are open, in-progress, completed, and overdue.
Downstream-party notification tasks track acknowledgement from the processor/third party, not just dispatch.

features.name: Stop/Purge Completion Receipts
features.description: Capture proof of completion for each action and issue the patient a court-ready receipt confirming what was stopped or purged and when.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want a verifiable receipt for every stop/purge action so that I can prove to the patient and the Board that the withdrawal was executed within time.
acceptanceCriteria: Each completed task records who completed it, when, and the action taken (stopped/purged/notified), with the completing owner's attestation.
When all in-scope tasks for a withdrawal are complete, the patient receives a confirmation receipt summarizing what was withdrawn and the actions taken.
A consolidated, tamper-evident withdrawal evidence package can be exported for any request showing the full timeline from intake to completion.
Downstream-party acknowledgements are included in the completion record.

features.name: Patient Withdrawal Status Tracker
features.description: Give the patient real-time visibility into their withdrawal request status and SLA countdown via the portal and proactive notifications.
features.userStory: As a patient, I want to see the status of my withdrawal request and when it will be completed so that I have confidence my data is actually being stopped.
acceptanceCriteria: The patient can view their request status (received, in progress, completed) using the reference number, on the portal and via SMS/notification.
Status and notifications are presented in the patient's chosen Eighth Schedule language.
The patient is proactively notified when the withdrawal is completed or if it is delayed beyond the committed timeframe.

features.name: Guardian & Assisted Withdrawal for Minors and Dependents
features.description: Allow a verified guardian or authorized representative to withdraw consent on behalf of a minor or dependent, with proof of authority captured.
features.userStory: As front-desk staff, I want to process a withdrawal made by a verified guardian for a minor so that we honor withdrawals for patients who cannot act for themselves while staying compliant.
acceptanceCriteria: A withdrawal can be submitted by a guardian/authorized representative only after their relationship and authority are verified and recorded.
The request record links the guardian's identity to the patient and notes that the withdrawal was guardian-initiated.
For minors, the same impact-analysis and execution flow applies as for adult withdrawals.

features.name: Re-consent & Reactivation Flow
features.description: Let a patient who previously withdrew a purpose easily grant it again, with the new consent treated as a fresh, separately logged permission.
features.userStory: As a patient, I want to re-grant consent I previously withdrew so that I can opt back into a service like research without confusion about my history.
acceptanceCriteria: A patient can re-consent to a previously withdrawn purpose without it overwriting or hiding the prior withdrawal record.
The reactivation is logged as a new consent event with its own timestamp, preserving the full withdraw-then-reconsent history.
Re-consent cannot silently reactivate purged data; the patient is informed if previously purged data cannot be recovered.

why: This module exists to satisfy the Data Fiduciary's DPDP Act 2023 accountability and demonstrable-compliance obligation (Sections 5, 8(1)/8(2), 8(7)) — when a patient complains or the Data Protection Board investigates, the hospital must be able to PROVE what permission existed, when, for what purpose, and that it was honored, with tamper-evident evidence that holds up in front of the Board and courts.

features.name: Tamper-Evident Permission Ledger
features.description: Append-only, hash-chained ledger that records every permission event (grant, scope, withdrawal, expiry, access) as an immutable entry.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want every permission event written to an append-only hash-chained ledger so that no record can be silently altered or deleted and I can defend the hospital's compliance posture.
acceptanceCriteria: Every permission lifecycle event (grant, modify, withdraw, expire, purpose-use) creates a new ledger entry; existing entries can never be edited or deleted, only superseded.
Each entry is cryptographically chained to the prior entry so any tampering breaks the chain and is detectable.
Entries are timestamped with a trusted time source and attributed to the actor (patient, staff member, or system) who caused the event.
An integrity-check function can confirm the entire chain is intact and flag the exact entry where any break occurs.

features.name: Regulator & Court-Ready Evidence Package Export
features.description: One-click generation of a self-contained, signed evidence bundle for a patient or incident, ready to hand to the Data Protection Board or a court.
features.userStory: As a DPO responding to a Board inquiry, I want to export a complete signed evidence package for a patient in one click so that I can prove our permission handling without engineering help or manual assembly.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can generate a package scoped to one patient, one consent reference, or one incident/date-range and receive a single downloadable bundle.
The package includes the signed permission artifacts, the relevant ledger timeline, integrity proof, and a plain-language summary cover sheet.
The exported package is digitally signed/sealed and includes verification instructions a third party can follow to confirm authenticity offline.
The act of exporting is itself recorded in the access log with requester, scope, and reason.

features.name: Per-Patient Permission Timeline
features.description: A single chronological view of everything that ever happened to a patient's permissions, retrievable by patient ID, ABHA, or consent reference.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want a complete chronological timeline of a patient's permissions so that I can answer 'what did we have permission to do, and when' in seconds during a grievance or audit.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can pull the full timeline by patient identifier, linked ABHA number, or consent reference and see all grants, scopes, purposes, withdrawals, and accesses in order.
Each timeline entry shows what changed, who triggered it, the purpose it was tied to, and the language the patient saw at capture.
Withdrawal events and the resulting state change are clearly visible alongside the grant they revoke.
The timeline view can be exported directly into an evidence package.

features.name: Fast Evidence Retrieval & Search
features.description: High-speed search and filter across the vault by patient, ABHA, consent reference, purpose, date range, or event type.
features.userStory: As a DPO under a time-bound Board notice, I want to locate the exact permission evidence I need by any identifier or filter so that I can respond within regulatory deadlines.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can search by patient identifier, ABHA, consent reference, purpose, actor, event type, or date range and combine filters.
Search returns results fast enough to use interactively during an active inquiry, even on a large historical vault.
Search results link directly to the underlying ledger entries and the patient timeline.
Searches that surface patient records are themselves logged in the vault access log.

features.name: Vault Access Logging (Watch-the-Watchers)
features.description: Immutable logging of every read, search, and export performed against the vault itself, so the evidence store is as accountable as the data it protects.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want every access to the evidence vault recorded immutably so that I can prove the audit trail was not misused and so the Board trusts the evidence as untampered.
acceptanceCriteria: Every view, search, and export against the vault records who accessed it, when, what scope, and the stated reason.
Access logs are written to the same append-only, tamper-evident store and cannot be edited by vault users including admins.
A DPO can review and export an access report for any time window or for a specific patient's records.

features.name: Integrity Proof & Verification
features.description: On-demand and scheduled integrity verification of the ledger, producing a portable proof that a given entry or package is genuine and unaltered.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want to produce a verifiable integrity proof for any record so that a regulator or opposing counsel can independently confirm our evidence was not tampered with.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can run an integrity check on the whole ledger or a selected subset and get a clear pass/fail with the location of any break.
A portable proof can be attached to any exported evidence package and verified by a third party without access to the live system.
Scheduled integrity checks run automatically and alert the DPO if the chain is ever found broken.

features.name: Retention & Lawful Disposal Alignment
features.description: Enforces retention rules so evidence is kept for the required period and disposed of in an auditable way, with the disposal itself logged as evidence.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want the vault to retain evidence for the mandated period and then dispose of it in a logged, provable way so that we meet both retention duties and the DPDP storage-limitation principle.
acceptanceCriteria: Each evidence class carries a configurable retention period aligned to applicable health-records and DPDP requirements.
Records past retention are flagged for review and disposed only through a controlled, logged action — never silently.
Disposal events are themselves written to the tamper-evident ledger as proof of lawful deletion, retaining a non-reversible record that disposal occurred.

features.name: Multi-Language Evidence Rendering
features.description: Renders the evidence package and patient timeline in the Eighth Schedule language the patient was served, plus an English working copy for the Board.
features.userStory: As a DPO, I want evidence to show the exact regional-language notice the patient actually saw, alongside an English version, so that a court can confirm informed permission for low-literacy or non-English-speaking patients.
acceptanceCriteria: Evidence packages preserve and display the original Eighth Schedule language version presented to the patient at capture.
An English working copy is generated alongside the original-language record for Board and court review.
The package clearly states which language version was the one the patient acted on.
